Hook: India now has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Caption or brief: The newest is Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026, where the Buddha is said to have given his first sermon. The first four were Agra Fort, the Taj Mahal, Ajanta and Ellora in 1983.

Hook: India now has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Caption or brief: The newest is Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026, where the Buddha is said to have given his first sermon. The first four were Agra Fort, the Taj Mahal, Ajanta and Ellora in 1983.

Hook: At Humayun's Tomb, look up at the dome twice.
Caption or brief: The outer dome and the inner ceiling are two separate shells. Stand inside, then outside, and you will see how the double dome lets the tomb look tall from afar and balanced from within.

Quick cuts from the Qutb, Tughlaqabad, Humayun's Tomb, Jama Masjid and India Gate, each with a date on screen. Line: one city, rebuilt again and again. End card: Delhi heritage walks, arranged on request.

Hook: Seven cities, one day.
Caption or brief: Our Delhi through seven cities programme picks the strongest stop from each capital, led by an archaeologist. For schools, teams and private groups.

Hook: Delhi's seven cities might be six, eight or eleven.
Caption or brief: It depends who is counting. Lal Kot and Qila Rai Pithora are sometimes one city; Jahanpanah was really a wall; New Delhi is often called the eighth.

Hook: One of the largest Harappan cities is about three hours from Delhi.
Caption or brief: Rakhigarhi in Haryana sits beside a living village, and its mounds hold early and mature Harappan layers. Most people have never heard of it.
A drone-style pan over Rakhigarhi mounds, then a close-up of a Harappan bead in a hand. On-screen line: 4,500 years ago this was a city. End card: Indus Valley Civilization facts for students.

Hook: How to read a timeline without getting lost.
Caption or brief: Anchor three dates: the mature Harappan cities around 2600 BCE, Ashoka around 250 BCE and the Cholas around 1000 CE. Place everything else before, between or after.

Hook: Take your class from the Stone Age to the Guptas.
Caption or brief: Our lectures and workshops teach ancient Indian history through tools, seals, inscriptions and coins. Online or at your school, arranged on request.

Hook: Learn to read temples like an architect.
Caption or brief: Our course on Indian temple architecture moves from first principles to regional styles. Run online or in person for groups, with optional study tours.
Split screen: a slow pan up the shikhara at Khajuraho beside a pan up the vimana at Thanjavur. On-screen line: 'Same purpose, two answers.' Ending card: Temple architecture with Talaash Heritage.

Hook: For centuries, nobody could read Ashoka.
Caption or brief: Brahmi was forgotten until James Prinsep cracked it in the 1830s, helped by a word repeated on the Sanchi railings: dānaṃ, 'gift'. Ancient Indian history changed overnight.

Hook: Learning Sanskrit? Finish one textbook.
Caption or brief: The most common mistake is sampling five courses and finishing none. Pick one complete grammar, add a spoken class for motivation, and read aloud every day.

Hook: Sanskrit nouns have a dual: one, two, and many.
Caption or brief: Devaḥ is one god, devau two gods, devāḥ many. It looks odd at first, then it starts to feel precise. Beginners meet it in their first month.

Hook: Thinking about a career in archaeology?
Caption or brief: Our career sessions cover courses, fieldwork and jobs in the ASI, museums, universities and heritage work. Online, for students and parents.
A day in the life montage: trench in the morning, pottery sorting at noon, report writing in the evening. On-screen line: 'Archaeology is more than digging.' End card: 'Archaeology career sessions.'

Hook: The Taj was built to be seen from a garden across the river.
Caption or brief: Mehtab Bagh, on the far bank of the Yamuna, sits on the same axis as the Taj. Excavations found its pools and walkways, and it shows how the tomb belongs to a whole river city of gardens.

Hook: The Taj was built to be seen from a garden across the river.
Caption or brief: Mehtab Bagh, on the far bank of the Yamuna, sits on the same axis as the Taj. Excavations found its pools and walkways, and it shows how the tomb belongs to a whole river city of gardens.

Hook: Go behind the Hawa Mahal.
Caption or brief: From the street it looks like a palace. From the back you see it is a screen only a room or so deep, built in 1799 so women of the court could watch processions unseen.

Shadow moving on the Samrat Yantra, then a drone-free street shot of the grid bazaar and the Hawa Mahal screen. Line: a city planned like an instrument. End card: Jaipur heritage walks, arranged on request.

Hook: Let your students dig, safely.
Caption or brief: Our mock excavation recreates a trench with layers and finds. Students dig, record and interpret, just as archaeologists do. Available for schools and colleges on request.

Hook: Let your students dig, safely.
Caption or brief: Our mock excavation recreates a trench with layers and finds. Students dig, record and interpret, just as archaeologists do. Available for schools and colleges on request.

Hook: Nearly every script in India descends from one ancestor.
Caption or brief: Devanagari, Tamil, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu and Sharada all grew out of Brahmi, the script of Ashoka's edicts. Look closely at a modern letter and you can sometimes still see its ancestor.

A hand tracing Brahmi letters on a printed copy of an Ashokan edict, then writing a student's name in the same letters. On-screen line: 'This script is 2,200 years old. You can learn it in an afternoon.' End card: 'Brahmi workshops for groups.'

Hook: Look up inside a Mughal dome.
Caption or brief: The ceiling is far lower than the outer dome. That gap is the double dome, a Timurid idea the Mughals made famous in India.

Hook: Two stepwells, one city.
Caption or brief: Walk Agrasen ki Baoli in central Delhi and Rajon ki Baoli in Mehrauli with an archaeologist. For schools, families and photography groups.

Hook: A stepwell is a building that goes down.
Caption or brief: Rani-ki-Vav in Patan descends seven levels to reach groundwater, with hundreds of carved figures on the way. It has been a World Heritage Site since 2014.

Hook: Delhi has an Ashokan edict in a residential colony.
Caption or brief: Near East of Kailash, a rock outcrop of the ridge carries a minor rock edict of Ashoka, more than two thousand years old.

Look up the Qutb Minar, cut to Humayun's Tomb through its gateway, then the Lahori Gate of the Red Fort. On-screen line: 'Three UNESCO sites, eight cities, one Delhi.' End card: 'Delhi heritage walks, on request.'

Hook: Delhi has an Ashokan edict still on its original rock.
Caption or brief: The minor rock edict at Srinivaspuri, near East of Kailash, sits in a small protected enclosure. Go with the ASI translation in hand and look for the neat rows of Brahmi.

Hook: The edict about the Kalinga war is missing in Kalinga.
Caption or brief: At Dhauli and Jaugada in Odisha, Rock Edict 13, with its regret for the slaughter, was left out. Separate edicts urging officials to treat local people fairly appear instead.

Hook: Varanasi and Sarnath with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange study tours to the ghats and Sarnath for schools, colleges, companies and families, in English or Hindi, on dates you choose.
Dawn boat shot along the ghats, then cut to the Dhamek Stupa and the Lion Capital. Line: a living river city and a 2,000 year old monastery, 10 km apart. End card: Varanasi and Sarnath study tours.

Hook: India now has 11 classical languages.
Caption or brief: Tamil was first in 2004. In October 2024 Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali joined Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia.

Hook: Pali and Prakrit are classical now. Want to read them?
Caption or brief: Our introductory Pali and Prakrit courses start from the script and reach real texts, and our lecture places all eleven languages in one story. For schools, colleges and adults.

Hook: At a painted shelter, step back before you step in.
Caption or brief: Look at the whole panel first and find the largest animals, then the smaller human figures. Avoid flash and never touch or wet the paint.
Slow pan across a painted shelter wall, pausing on a bison, then a line of dancers, then a horse rider. On-screen line: 'Three periods, one wall.' End card: 'Read rock art with an archaeologist.'

Hook: Walk Fort with someone who reads buildings for a living.
Caption or brief: We arrange Mumbai heritage walks for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, led by an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi. Tell us your date and group size.

Hook: Most Indian archaeologists did not study archaeology at BA level.
Caption or brief: The usual route is a BA in history or a related subject, then an MA in archaeology or ancient Indian history, culture and archaeology. Science graduates can come in too.

Hook: Most Indian archaeologists did not study archaeology at BA level.
Caption or brief: The usual route is a BA in history or a related subject, then an MA in archaeology or ancient Indian history, culture and archaeology. Science graduates can come in too.

Hook: A coin in a layer tells you its minimum age, not its exact age.
Caption or brief: Coins circulated for years, sometimes centuries. Archaeologists use them to say a floor is no older than the coin, then cross-check with pottery and scientific dates.

Close-up of a trench wall with layers marked by labels. On-screen line: 'The deeper you dig, the further back you go. Usually.' Cut to a pit cutting through the layers. End card: 'Chronology and dating, for schools and colleges.'

Hook: Hampi with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange Hampi trips for schools, colleges and private groups, often with Badami and Pattadakal, in English or Hindi.

Hook: The stepped tank at Hampi was found in the 1980s.
Caption or brief: Excavations in the Royal Centre uncovered a perfectly symmetrical tank of cut granite. Marks on the blocks suggest they were assembled to a plan, possibly brought from elsewhere.

Hook: A Gupta-period iron pillar has stood in the open for about 1,600 years.
Caption or brief: The iron pillar at the Qutb complex carries an inscription of a king named Chandra. Metallurgists have studied why it rusts so little.
The Varaha panel at Udayagiri filmed from left to right, then a cut to Temple 17 at Sanchi. Line: where Indian temple building began. End card: Gupta art and architecture explained.

Hook: At the Qutb, look at the pillars, not just the minar.
Caption or brief: The colonnades of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque reuse carved temple pillars, and the mosque's own inscription says so. It is a lesson in how monuments record history.

Hook: Five dynasties, two mornings.
Caption or brief: Our Qutb complex and Tughlaqabad walks cover the whole Sultanate. For schools, colleges, teams and private groups.

Hook: Teach your students to listen like anthropologists.
Caption or brief: Our oral history lab trains students to interview elders, record memories and write them up with care. Run at schools and colleges on request.

A student holding a phone recorder sits with an elderly shopkeeper in an old market; cut to handwritten field notes. On-screen line: 'Every neighbourhood is an archive.' Ending card: Oral history labs with Talaash Heritage.

Hook: Ashoka did not write in Sanskrit.
Caption or brief: His edicts are in Prakrit, the spoken language of his time, written mostly in Brahmi. Sanskrit inscriptions only become common a few centuries later.

Hook: Look up for the chabutro.
Caption or brief: Almost every pol has a carved bird feeder on a pillar. Read its date and inscription and you often learn who paid for it and when. Go before 8 am when the lanes are quiet.

Hook: Ahmedabad was India's first World Heritage City.
Caption or brief: UNESCO did not list one monument in 2017. It listed a whole walled city: Sultanate mosques and the pols around them, lived in since 1411.

Hook: Amritsar with a historian.
Caption or brief: We arrange Amritsar study tours for schools, colleges, companies and families, from the Gurus to Partition, in English or Hindi.

Reflection of Harmandir Sahib in the tank, then the narrow lane into Jallianwala Bagh and a quiet frame in the Partition Museum. Line: one walk, four centuries. End card: Amritsar study tours, arranged on request.

Hook: Badami Cave 3 is dated to the year.
Caption or brief: An inscription in the cave gives 578 CE, under the Chalukya king Mangalesha. Dated monuments this early are rare in India, which makes the cave a fixed point for art historians.

Hook: Badami Cave 3 is dated to the year.
Caption or brief: An inscription in the cave gives 578 CE, under the Chalukya king Mangalesha. Dated monuments this early are rare in India, which makes the cave a fixed point for art historians.

Hook: Look for the second layer.
Caption or brief: At any monument, ask what still happens there: prayer, music, a market, a festival. That living layer is intangible heritage, and it is part of the site.
Quick cuts between a Mughal tomb, a handloom, a folk song and a festival street. On screen: All of this is cultural heritage. End card: Learn what heritage means, with Talaash Heritage.

Hook: Learn conservation the right way.
Caption or brief: Our workshops on preventive conservation and heritage documentation are arranged for colleges, museums and groups, online or in person.

Hook: Learn conservation the right way.
Caption or brief: Our workshops on preventive conservation and heritage documentation are arranged for colleges, museums and groups, online or in person.

Hook: Garba is on a UNESCO list.
Caption or brief: In 2023 the Garba of Gujarat joined India's entries on UNESCO's intangible heritage list, alongside Kumbh Mela, Yoga and Durga Puja in Kolkata. Heritage can be a dance as much as a monument.

Close shots of hands: a potter's wheel, a dancer's feet, a weaver's shuttle, a priest's chanting lips. On screen: You cannot fence this heritage. You can only pass it on. End card: Intangible heritage explained, Talaash Heritage.

Hook: Look at the repairs, not just the monument.
Caption or brief: Next time you visit a monument, find where it has been repaired. Lime or cement? Matching stone or not? Repairs tell you how a building has been cared for, and sometimes how it was harmed.

Hook: Travel with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: TALAASHH plans study tours and private journeys for schools, colleges and small groups, from the Golden Triangle to the forts of Rajasthan.

Hook: India now has 45 World Heritage Sites.
Caption or brief: The newest is Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026. How many have you visited? Tell us your count.

Hook: The Red Fort has two stories.
Caption or brief: One is history: Shah Jahan's palace, 1857, a British garrison. The other is heritage: the Independence Day speech. Same walls, different questions.
Split screen: an inscription on the Qutb Minar on one side, tourists taking selfies on the other. On screen: History asks what happened. Heritage asks what it means now. End card: Talaash Heritage.

Hook: Hand block or screen print?
Caption or brief: Turn the fabric over. Hand block prints often show slight overlaps and colour variation at the repeat. That small irregularity is the mark of the hand.

Hook: Bidriware is black for a reason.
Caption or brief: Craftsmen in Bidar blacken a zinc alloy with a special soil paste, so the silver inlay shines against it. The craft holds a GI tag.

Hook: Bengaluru, older than you think.
Caption or brief: We arrange heritage walks in the pete, Basavanagudi and Cubbon Park for schools, colleges and companies. In English or Hindi, on your dates.
Time-lapse of Avenue Road traffic, then a still shot of the fort gateway. On-screen line: 'This city had a fort before it had flyovers.' End card: 'Heritage walks in Bengaluru, arranged on request.'

Hook: For 107 years, Bhopal was ruled by women.
Caption or brief: From 1819 to 1926 four Begums governed Bhopal state. Their mosques, palaces and markets still shape the old city around the lake.

Hook: Bhopal is a base for 30,000 years of history.
Caption or brief: We arrange walks in old Bhopal and trips to Sanchi, Bhimbetka and Bhojpur for schools, colleges and private groups, with an archaeologist, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Find the elephant at Dhauli.
Caption or brief: Above Ashoka's edicts, an elephant emerges from the rock. It is one of the earliest rock-cut sculptures in India. Read the edict first, then look up.
Quick cuts from temple to temple in date order, the tower growing each time. On-screen line: 'Watch a temple grow over 400 years.' End card: 'Bhubaneswar heritage walks, arranged on request.'

Hook: Bodh Gaya and Nalanda with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange Buddhist heritage visits in Bihar for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Chandigarh's first plan was not by Le Corbusier.
Caption or brief: Albert Mayer and Matthew Nowicki drew the first master plan. Le Corbusier took over in 1951 and turned it into the grid of sectors we see today.

Hook: Chandigarh's first plan was not by Le Corbusier.
Caption or brief: Albert Mayer and Matthew Nowicki drew the first master plan. Le Corbusier took over in 1951 and turned it into the grid of sectors we see today.

Hook: Walk round the tank before you enter the temple.
Caption or brief: At Kapaleeshwarar in Mylapore, the tank, the market and the gopuram work as one public space. Start at the steps and watch how people use them.
Open on the Kapaleeshwarar gopuram at dawn, cut to the bronze gallery at Egmore. On-screen line: 'Chennai is older than Madras.' End card: 'Heritage walks in Chennai, arranged on request.'

Hook: Ajanta and Ellora with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange heritage trips to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Ellora and Ajanta for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Ellora's Kailasa was carved from the top down.
Caption or brief: Under the Rashtrakutas in the 8th century, carvers cut a whole temple out of a basalt hill, starting from above. Nothing was added; everything was taken away.

Hook: In 1671 the Ahoms beat a Mughal fleet on the Brahmaputra at Guwahati.
Caption or brief: The Battle of Saraighat, led by Lachit Borphukan, was fought on the river itself. It is one of the few major river battles in Indian history.

Ferry ride to Umananda at golden hour, then the museum's Kamarupa sculpture. On-screen line: 'The northeast has a history your textbook skipped.' End card: 'Guwahati heritage walks, arranged on request.'

Hook: Look for the ducks on Man Mandir.
Caption or brief: The palace front carries glazed tiles of ducks, elephants and banana trees in blue, green and yellow. Stand back on the road below to see the whole frieze.

Hook: Gwalior, Orchha and Khajuraho in one tour.
Caption or brief: We arrange central India study tours for schools, colleges, companies and families, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Golconda and the old city with a historian.
Caption or brief: We arrange Hyderabad heritage walks for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, in English or Hindi, on dates that suit you.

Film a clap at the Golconda gate, then cut to the summit where someone raises a hand on hearing it. On-screen line: 'A 16th century alarm system.' End card: 'Heritage walks in Hyderabad, arranged on request.'

Hook: People still live inside Jaisalmer Fort.
Caption or brief: Founded in 1156, the fort is a UNESCO site and a neighbourhood at once. That is wonderful, and a real conservation problem: water and drains do not mix well with 850 year old walls.

Hook: Walk down from Mehrangarh, not up.
Caption or brief: Drive to the fort, spend two hours inside, then walk down through Brahmpuri to Toorji ka Jhalra. Easier on the legs and you see the city unfold below you.

Hook: Nobody knows for sure why Jodhpur is blue.
Caption or brief: Indigo in lime wash, caste custom, cooler walls, fewer insects: every guide has a reason. On our walks we treat it as a question, and let students weigh the evidence.

Hook: Khajuraho, read like an architect.
Caption or brief: Our Khajuraho deep dive and central India study tours are arranged for schools, colleges, companies and families, with an archaeologist, in English or Hindi.

Slow tilt up the Kandariya Mahadeva tower, close-ups of musicians and elephants on the frieze, then the Parshvanatha temple. Line: a mountain range in stone. End card: Khajuraho study tours, arranged on request.

Hook: Vasco da Gama's gravestone is still in Kochi.
Caption or brief: He died here in 1524 and was buried in St Francis Church. His body went back to Portugal, but the original stone stayed.

Hook: Vasco da Gama's gravestone is still in Kochi.
Caption or brief: He died here in 1524 and was buried in St Francis Church. His body went back to Portugal, but the original stone stayed.

Hook: Read a cemetery like a document.
Caption or brief: At South Park Street Cemetery, note the age at death, the profession and who paid for the stone. Within an hour you will see who came to Calcutta, and how many did not leave.
Film the walk from St John's Church to the GPO dome in one slow take. On-screen line: 'You are standing on a fort that no longer exists.' End card: 'Heritage walks in Kolkata, arranged on request.'

Hook: Ladakh, planned properly.
Caption or brief: We arrange Leh study tours for schools, colleges, companies and families, with acclimatisation built in and an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Ladakh, planned properly.
Caption or brief: We arrange Leh study tours for schools, colleges, companies and families, with acclimatisation built in and an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Hook: The Bara Imambara was a famine relief project.
Caption or brief: Asaf-ud-Daula began it in 1784, a famine year, and the building gave paid work to thousands. Its vaulted hall is built in brick and lime, with no beams holding up the roof.
Walk through the Rumi Darwaza, up into the Bhool Bhulaiya, then a close shot of shell marks at the Residency. Line: one city, two stories. End card: Lucknow heritage walks, arranged on request.

Hook: Leave your phone on the bus.
Caption or brief: Phones are not allowed in the Meenakshi Temple. Without one, groups actually look at the ceilings, the painted corridors and the pillars.

Hook: Mahabalipuram with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: Our Mamallapuram programme is arranged for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi, as a day trip or part of a study tour.

Hook: Each of the Five Rathas copies a different kind of building.
Caption or brief: A thatched hut, a barrel-vaulted hall, a stepped tower: the Pallava sculptors carved a catalogue of architecture from single boulders.

Hook: Mysore Palace is younger than the Eiffel Tower.
Caption or brief: The present palace was finished in 1912, after a fire in 1897 destroyed the older wooden one. Its style is a deliberate blend, built to present a modern princely state.
A slow pan across the Daria Daulat Bagh battle mural, cut to the Somanathapura star plan from above. On-screen line: 'Three centuries in one day out of Mysuru.' End card: 'Arranged on request.'

Hook: Look at the walls of Bom Jesus.
Caption or brief: The facade is bare red laterite because the lime plaster was stripped in the 20th century. Compare it with Se Cathedral across the road, still plastered white.

Hook: Old Goa was once bigger than Lisbon, by some accounts.
Caption or brief: In the 16th century it was the capital of Portuguese Asia. Epidemics and a silting river emptied it, and only the churches remained in the fields.

Hook: Orchha with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange Orchha visits within central India study tours, with Gwalior and Khajuraho, for schools, colleges, companies and families, in English or Hindi.

Climb through Jahangir Mahal to a balcony view, then the Chaturbhuj spires and the chhatris at dusk. Line: a whole 17th century royal town, still standing. End card: Orchha study tours, arranged on request.

Hook: Ashoka's capital is under Patna's streets.
Caption or brief: Pataliputra was the capital of the Mauryan empire. Most of it lies beneath the modern city; Kumhrar is one of the few places you can see it excavated.

Hook: Patna and Nalanda with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange heritage walks in Patna and trips to Nalanda and Rajgir for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi.

Hook: At Khusro Bagh, look up.
Caption or brief: The ceilings of the tombs have painted and carved Mughal decoration. Bring students into the centre of each tomb and ask them to sketch what is overhead.
Boat at the Sangam, the fort walls, Khusro Bagh's domes and Anand Bhavan's verandah. Line: from Ashoka to the freedom movement in one city. End card: Prayagraj study tours, arranged on request.

Hook: Puducherry with a historian.
Caption or brief: We arrange heritage walks in White Town, the Tamil quarter and Arikamedu for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Pune's streets are named after the days of the week.
Caption or brief: Shaniwar, Budhwar, Somwar, Raviwar: the old peths were market quarters, each with its own weekly market day. The city grew around them in the 18th century.

Hook: Pune's streets are named after the days of the week.
Caption or brief: Shaniwar, Budhwar, Somwar, Raviwar: the old peths were market quarters, each with its own weekly market day. The city grew around them in the 18th century.

Hook: Look at the roofs, not just the fronts.
Caption or brief: Steep tin roofs and timber frames were Shimla's answer to snow, rain and earthquakes. Walk the Mall and count the ways builders handled the slope.
Toy train crossing a bridge, then the Ridge, Christ Church and the Viceregal Lodge. Line: the summer capital of an empire. End card: Shimla study tours, arranged on request.

Hook: Srinagar with a historian.
Caption or brief: We arrange Srinagar study tours for schools, colleges, companies and families, from the old city to the gardens, in English or Hindi.

Hook: Srinagar's Jamia Masjid stands on 378 wooden columns.
Caption or brief: Each is a single deodar trunk. Built around 1400 and rebuilt after fires, the mosque shows Kashmir's own timber tradition.

Hook: The Big Temple's walls are a Chola account book.
Caption or brief: Inscriptions around its base list gifts of land, gold and cattle, and the names of hundreds of temple staff. It is one of the best documented buildings of medieval India.
Close-up of a Chola inscription, then pull back to the full vimana. On-screen line: 'Every gift was written on the wall.' End card: 'Thanjavur heritage walks, arranged on request.'

Hook: Read Udaipur from the water.
Caption or brief: From a boat on Lake Pichola the City Palace looks like a fortress on one side and a pleasure palace on the other. Then walk the ghats to see how ordinary people used the same lake.

Hook: Udaipur and the Mewar forts, with an archaeologist.
Caption or brief: We arrange heritage walks in Udaipur and trips to Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi.

Hook: The Adil Shahi capital with a historian.
Caption or brief: We arrange heritage walks in Vijayapura for schools, colleges and private groups, in English or Hindi, and can link it with Badami and Pattadakal.

Sound-led reel: a whisper recorded in the gallery, then the camera pulls back to show the full dome from outside, then cut to Ibrahim Rauza. On-screen line: 'Built to carry a whisper.' End card: 'Vijayapura heritage walks, on request.'

Hook: Thai, Tibetan and Tamil scripts share one ancestor.
Caption or brief: Nearly every script of South and Southeast Asia grew out of Brahmi, the script of Ashoka's edicts. The shapes changed; the sound order did not.

Hook: Learn to draw a hand axe in ten seconds.
Caption or brief: Prehistory answers are clearer with a quick sketch: a hand axe, a cleaver, a microlith, a polished Neolithic axe. Practise them until they are automatic. It saves time in the hall.

Hook: The anthropology optional is two papers, 250 marks each.
Caption or brief: Paper I is the discipline as a whole: evolution, prehistory, kinship, theory. Paper II is India: prehistory, caste, villages and tribal communities. Our guide breaks down both.

Hook: Walk a protected site with someone who can read it.
Caption or brief: Our walks at Mehrauli Archaeological Park and Purana Qila show excavation and conservation in practice. For schools, colleges and private groups.

Close-up of a blue ASI board, pull back to reveal the monument behind it. On-screen line: 'Since 1861, someone has been looking after this.' End card: 'Walk protected monuments with an archaeologist.'

Hook: India's oldest museum opened in 1814.
Caption or brief: The Indian Museum in Kolkata grew out of the Asiatic Society's collections. Its Bharhut gateway and railing are among the earliest major pieces of Indian sculpture.

Hook: India's oldest museum opened in 1814.
Caption or brief: The Indian Museum in Kolkata grew out of the Asiatic Society's collections. Its Bharhut gateway and railing are among the earliest major pieces of Indian sculpture.

Hook: See all four branches in one museum visit.
Caption or brief: At a good ethnographic museum, look at the tools (archaeology), the textiles and ritual objects (cultural), the labels in local languages (linguistic) and any displays on food and health (biological). The links appear quickly.

Four quick cuts: a replica hand axe, a skull cast, a market conversation being recorded, a page of handwritten words in two scripts. On-screen line: 'Four ways to study one species.' Ending card: 'Branches of anthropology, explained.'

Hook: A Buddhist monastery inside Mumbai city limits.
Caption or brief: Kanheri has over a hundred caves, cisterns and stairways. We lead guided visits for schools and groups, with an optional lecture on rock-cut architecture beforehand.

Hook: A Buddhist monastery inside Mumbai city limits.
Caption or brief: Kanheri has over a hundred caves, cisterns and stairways. We lead guided visits for schools and groups, with an optional lecture on rock-cut architecture beforehand.

Hook: A Tamil village chose its committee by lottery in about 920 CE.
Caption or brief: Inscriptions at Uttaramerur describe names written on palm leaves, put in a pot and drawn by a child. They also list who could not stand: for example, those who had not submitted accounts.
Low-angle shot of the Thanjavur vimana against the sky, cut to a Chola bronze Nataraja in a museum case. Line: built a thousand years ago, still in worship. End card: The Chola dynasty, explained.

Hook: Find the dancers on temple walls.
Caption or brief: At Konark and Bhubaneswar, look for the tribhanga pose, the three bends of the body. You will see Odissi frozen in stone.

Hook: Fieldwork is best learnt by doing.
Caption or brief: Our oral history lab teaches interviewing, consent and note-taking to anthropology and sociology students. It runs online or on your campus, anywhere in India.

Hook: M. N. Srinivas is claimed by both anthropology and sociology.
Caption or brief: His study of a Karnataka village and his idea of Sanskritisation shaped both subjects in India. That is how close the two disciplines are here. Read our guide to the real differences.

Hook: For most of human time in India, there was no writing at all.
Caption or brief: Everything we know about those hundreds of thousands of years comes from archaeology: stone tools, rock paintings and the remains of camps. History, in the strict sense, starts very late.

Split screen: on the left, a hand turning the page of a printed chronicle; on the right, a trowel scraping a soil section. On-screen line: 'Same past, two kinds of evidence.' End card: 'Archaeology and history, explained by archaeologists.'

Hook: At a Harappan site, look down, not up.
Caption or brief: The walls are low, but the drains, wells and street lines are the real story. Trace where water went and you understand how the city worked.

Hook: Some of the world's oldest hand axes were found near Chennai.
Caption or brief: Acheulian tools from Attirampakkam have been dated to around 1.5 million years ago. India's archaeological record starts far earlier than most people imagine.

Hook: Document a living tradition.
Caption or brief: Our oral history and neighbourhood memory lab helps students record folk dances, songs and festivals carefully and with consent.
A map of India fills state by state with a two-second clip of each folk dance. On screen: One country, hundreds of dances. Which is yours? End card: Folk dances of India state-wise, Talaash Heritage.

Hook: The Panchatantra travelled from India to Europe.
Caption or brief: Its animal fables were translated into Middle Persian, then Arabic, then many European languages. Our guide to Indian folklore covers the great story collections and the oral epics still sung today.

Hook: Turn family stories into a class podcast.
Caption or brief: Our oral history lab and storytelling studio help students record, edit and share stories with care and consent. Sessions run online or at your school or college.

Hook: Count the turns at the gate.
Caption or brief: Sharp bends between gateways slowed attackers and stopped elephants charging. Next time you enter a fort, count them.
Drone-style rise over a hill fort wall, then cut to a close-up of a spiked gate. On screen: Every gate, wall and tank is a defence decision. End card: Forts of India, Talaash Heritage.

Hook: Let your students run their own dig.
Caption or brief: Our mock excavation gives a class a practice trench to excavate, record and interpret, with no harm to a real site. At your school or a venue nearby.

Hook: One inscription, three exam facts.
Caption or brief: The Prayaga prashasti is a Sanskrit eulogy of Samudragupta, written by Harishena, carved on an Ashokan pillar. Learn it that way and it answers three kinds of question.

Hook: One inscription, three exam facts.
Caption or brief: The Prayaga prashasti is a Sanskrit eulogy of Samudragupta, written by Harishena, carved on an Ashokan pillar. Learn it that way and it answers three kinds of question.

Hook: Learn eight dates and the rest of the timeline falls into place.
Caption or brief: 2600 BCE, 321 BCE, 320 CE, 1206, 1526, 1757, 1857, 1947. Hang every dynasty on one of these anchors and attach a monument to each. It sticks far better than a list.

Fast cuts of a hand axe, a Harappan seal, an Ashokan inscription, a Gupta coin, the Qutb Minar and the Red Fort, each with a date on screen. Line: one country, five thousand years, eight dates to remember. End card: Indian history timeline, full table on our site.

Hook: Learn to read a medieval Kashmiri manuscript.
Caption or brief: Our Sharada script course teaches the letters scribes used for Sanskrit in Kashmir. For colleges and adult learners, online or in person.

Hook: India's books were long and narrow because of palm leaves.
Caption or brief: The pothi format came from the shape of the leaf. Even when paper arrived, scribes kept the same shape for centuries.

Hook: The first Qutb arches are not real arches.
Caption or brief: The screen of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque was built by corbelling, stepping stones inward. True arches arrived a few decades later, at Balban's tomb.

Close-ups in order: a corbelled arch at the Qutb, a true arch at the Alai Darwaza, a Lodi double dome. On screen: How India learned to build the arch. End card: Indo-Islamic architecture, Talaash Heritage.

Hook: Remember why Magadha won with four words: rice, iron, rivers, elephants.
Caption or brief: Fertile land, iron ore to the south, capitals protected by hills and rivers, and war elephants from the eastern forests. Then add ambitious kings.

Hook: Hold a 2,500-year-old coin design in your hand.
Caption or brief: Our numismatics session uses replica punch-marked coins to show how India's earliest money worked. For schools and colleges.

Hook: Follow the dynasties gallery by gallery.
Caption or brief: Our museum mornings at the National Museum take a group from Mauryan to Chola objects with an archaeologist. Arranged for schools, colleges and adults.

Close-ups of coins in sequence: punch-marked, Kushana gold, Gupta gold, a Chola copper, each with the dynasty name on screen. Line: every dynasty signed its money. End card: Major dynasties of ancient India, full table.
